summary: DST variable interpolation causes composite alert eval drift in dashboards
description:
Issue summary: After the US DST forward shift (2026-03-14 in some regions) several enterprise customers reported missing and spurious alert notifications from composite dashboard panels (multi-query alert rules).

Impact: Nimbus Payments reports missed fraud-alerting notifications during a 2-hour window; they saw both an absence of expected alerts and duplicate firing shortly after. Multiple orgs in us-east showed temporal mismatches between trace-linked spans and alert evaluation windows.

Environment: production, affected regions us-east primarily with some spillover in eu-west where org timezone settings are non-UTC. Reported after recent timezone-service v2.4 rollout.

Observed behavior: Composite alerts that combine multiple panel queries using relative variables (eg. ${dashboard.time.start}, ${org.timezone_shift}) evaluated against server-local time boundaries, but dashboard variable interpolation for panel display used the org-configured timezone. The mismatch causes the alert-eval engine to construct an evaluation window that is offset by one hour in DST transitions, which in turn mis-buckets metric rollups and misattributes trace anchors.

Quick notes: This is not a general ingestion or rollup lag — single-panel alerts evaluated correctly when pinned to UTC or when not using dashboard variables. The problem manifests when: composite alert rules reference interpolated dashboard variables AND the org timezone differs from server-local time during DST boundary crossing.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dashboard with org timezone set to America/New_York
2) Add two panels: A) 1-min rate of error responses, B) 5-min p50 latency; each panel displays using ${dashboard.time.start} relative variables
3) Create a composite alert that triggers when A > 0.5 AND B > 300 using the dashboard variables for the evaluation window
4) Simulate traffic across the DST-forward boundary (advance system clock for a test node or run synthetic job spanning the boundary),
5) Observe alerting history: missing alert during the boundary hour then duplicate alerts once server-local eval aligns back
6) Compare single-panel alert with equivalent absolute window (no variables) — it evaluates correctly.
logs: 2026-03-12T15:07:12Z WARN alert-eval engine: eval_window_constructed start=2026-03-14T01:00:00-05:00 end=2026-03-14T01:05:00-05:00 org_tz=America/New_York server_time=UTC
comments: 2026-03-12 — Nimbus Support (J. Patel): 'We missed three fraud alerts between 01:00 and 02:00 local time. After that we saw the same alerts duplicated twice. This correlates with our org timezone being America/New_York.'

2026-03-12 — Aisha Khan (Support): 'Thanks for the report — escalating to SRE and alerting team. Can you provide a link to the dashboard and a sample API key we can use for read-only repro? Also requested retention/ingest timeline.'

2026-03-12 — Michael Chen (SRE): 'I reproduced locally with a synthetic job. The engine constructs eval windows using server UTC arithmetic; dashboard UI shows org TZ. Likely a variable interpolation boundary bug introduced in timezone-service v2.4.'

2026-03-13 — Engineering (L. Gómez): 'Adding more detail: the substitution layer returns a string timestamp without tz metadata; downstream eval builds a window using process.startOfMinute(server_time) which ignores org offset during DST shift. Preparing a patch.'
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Variable interpolation lost timezone metadata on formatted timestamps; downstream consumers assumed UTC.
Hypothesis 2: Alert-eval aggregation buckets use server-local 'startOf' semantics rather than normalized org-based bucketing during DST edges.
Reproduction: Local repro with container clock set to UTC and dashboard org_tz set to America/New_York reproduced both missed and duplicate alerts.
Observed correlation with timezone-service v2.4: PR #7294 modified timestamp formatting logic to simplify client display; change removed tz suffix in the interpolation payload.
Telemetry: Pagerduty and email alert logs show clustered duplicate messages at 01:58 and 02:03 local time; dashboards for affected orgs show evaluation windows off by 1 hour for composite rules.
resolution_notes: Mitigations applied: rolled back timezone-service v2.4 to v2.3 for org-facing interpolation endpoint in us-east while a fix is prepared (rollback completed 2026-03-13T08:30Z).

Short-term workaround for customers: edit dashboard and set timezone to UTC OR change composite alert rule to use absolute time windows (no ${dashboard.time.*} variables). Provided step-by-step to Nimbus support.

Planned fix: ensure variable interpolation payload includes explicit timezone offset and update alert-eval to normalize evaluation windows using org-configured timezone before bucketization. PR in progress: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/7341
Postmortem tasks: add unit tests for DST edge cases, add integration test in e2e-alerting that simulates DST transitions, update runbook for DST deployments.
